{
  "approach": "query",
  "change": "Refactor app/db.py to optimize the list_notes function by replacing the INSTR-based tag filtering with a normalized many-to-many note_tags table. 1) Add a new table 'note_tags' with columns (note_id INTEGER, tag TEXT) and a unique index on (note_id, tag). 2) Modify create_note to insert the note, then insert rows into note_tags for each tag. 3) Modify update_note to delete existing tags for the note_id and insert new ones. 4) Modify delete_note to delete associated note_tags. 5) Rewrite list_notes to use a JOIN between notes and note_tags for tag filtering (WHERE note_tags.tag = ?) and standard LIKE for search_text, using GROUP BY notes.id to handle duplicates from the join. This replaces the O(N*M) string scan with an O(log N) index lookup.",
  "hypothesis": "The current profile shows list_notes is the hottest path, and the existing tag filtering uses INSTR(tags, ?) which performs a linear string scan on every row. By normalizing tags into a separate indexed table, tag lookups become index-based joins, which are significantly faster for SQLite, especially as the number of notes or tags grows. This reduces the cumulative time in list_notes by avoiding full-table string scans for tag matching.",
  "risks": [
    "The implementation must correctly enforce the 'ALL tags' filter logic using GROUP BY and HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT tag) = number_of_tags, ensuring that notes with only a subset of the requested tags are excluded.",
    "The JOIN operation may produce duplicate rows for notes with multiple matching tags, requiring careful handling with GROUP BY and potentially affecting the total count query if not structured correctly.",
    "Write operations (create, update, delete) will incur additional overhead due to maintaining the junction table, which may offset read gains if the workload is write-heavy or the dataset is small.",
    "Schema migration for existing databases is not required as the runner uses a fresh database, but the initialization logic must ensure the new table is created before any operations."
  ],
  "schema_version": 1
}
